scams.name: HCMC Tan Son Nhat Airport (SGN) Fake-Grab Driver Scam
scams.description: Ho Chi Minh City's Tan Son Nhat Airport (SGN) has a 2025-documented epidemic of fake-Grab-driver scams that mirrors the Hanoi Noi Bai pattern. r/VietNam 'HCMC Airport (Grab prentending) taxi Scam' (comments/1p3puug, 2025) is a named 2025 first-person anchor; r/VietNam 'Robbed at HCM airport by fake Grab driver. Be' (comments/1js1uqh, 2025) adds context about the counter-measures now in place: 'It's such a successful scam that's why Grab and Be set up personnel at the pickup' zones — but scammers still operate inside the terminal. r/VietNam 'Double scammed by cab pretending to be Grab in Saigon' (comments/1n2j3b3, 2025) documents the compound pattern: fake Grab + overcharged meter. r/VietNam 'Airport experience with Taxi arrangement- HCMC' (comments/1p9dhcb, 2025) captures a 2025 variant with menace: 'This felt like a planned scam and could have been dangerous. Always double-check the car number and' licence plate. r/VietNam 'HCMC taxi scam, a cautionary tale (with a happy ending)' (comments/dzk58l) and r/VietNam 'HCMC - scams, scams and not scams' (comments/1os81k3, 2025) round out the community-documented HCMC airport-arrival patterns: drivers quote 'fixed prices' of 600,000–1,000,000 VND for rides that should cost 150,000–250,000 VND on the meter or Grab app. The legitimate fare from Tan Son Nhat to District 1 (central HCMC) is 150,000–200,000 VND by licensed Vinasun (Gold/Red branding) or Mai Linh (Green branding) on the meter, or 150,000–230,000 VND via Grab/Be app. For older travellers, the defence: (1) book Grab or Be yourself on airport Wi-Fi AFTER you have your luggage — verify licence plate matches app before entering; (2) use only Vinasun or Mai Linh licensed taxis with meter; (3) the official Grab/Be pickup counter is on the far side of the car park exit — wait there, not at arrivals; (4) IGNORE every person in the arrivals hall offering 'taxi' or 'Grab' — all are unauthorised per r/VietNam 'Scammed by a local driver' (comments/1s1bw6x, 2025); (5) the 152 public bus runs SGN to Ben Thanh for 5,000 VND but is slow and luggage-unfriendly.
scams.avoidance: Book Grab or Be yourself on airport Wi-Fi AFTER luggage — verify licence plate Use only Vinasun (Gold/Red) or Mai Linh (Green) licensed taxis with meter Wait at the official Grab/Be pickup counter past car park exit — not arrivals hall Ignore EVERY person in the arrivals hall offering 'taxi' or 'Grab' — all are unauthorised Typical fare to District 1: 150K–230K VND; anything over 400K is overcharging
scams.location: Tan Son Nhat International Airport (SGN) arrivals hall, unofficial pickup zones away from the official Grab/Be pickup counter, car-park exit driveways

scams.name: HCMC Street Taxi Meter Tampering & Vinasun Copycats
scams.description: Once past the airport, HCMC's street taxi problem mirrors Hanoi: meter tampering, fake-Vinasun and fake-Mai Linh copycats, and route skimming. r/VietNam 'HCMC taxi scam, a cautionary tale (with a happy ending)' (comments/dzk58l) documents the classic Vinasun copycat problem — taxis with livery that looks 'Vinasun' but are actually independent operators with tampered meters. The genuine Vinasun fleet is white with a distinctive red-and-gold stripe and phone number 1900-1055; Mai Linh is green with phone 1055. Copycats use near-identical colours and phone numbers with single-digit differences. r/VietNam 'Taxi scam' (comments/1h7s5b4, 2024) warns: 'You're lucky it's just a $20 taxi scam; you could have been' worse off. r/VietNam 'Late night encounter with Grab/Xanh SM' (comments/1i6uvaz, 2025) captures the 2025 'bait and switch' where a Grab driver cancels the app booking and suggests 'off-app' payment at a higher rate. r/VietNam 'Will you trust a grab driver offer to drive you not using their' (comments/1ozwdeu, 2025) confirms the off-app scam pattern: 'That is one of the scam method. Easy way to fix this is to simply enter your destination on the Grab app and insist on the app-booked fare. For older travellers, the practical defence: (1) use Grab or Be app for every ride — app-regulated fares and digital receipts; (2) if taking a street taxi, use only genuine Vinasun (white/red/gold, 1900-1055) or Mai Linh (green, 1055) — verify the phone number on the door; (3) insist on the meter before the car moves; (4) typical District 1 rides: 30,000–80,000 VND; anything over 150,000 VND is overcharging; (5) photograph the taxi licence plate from the rear windscreen; (6) for late-night returns from Bui Vien, pre-book Grab rather than hailing on the street; (7) refuse any 'off-app' deal offered by a Grab driver — re-book within the app per r/VietNam (comments/1ozwdeu, 2025).
scams.avoidance: Use Grab or Be app for every ride — app-regulated, digital receipts For street taxis, use ONLY Vinasun (1900-1055) or Mai Linh (1055) — verify phone number on door Insist on meter running before car moves Typical District 1 rides: 30K–80K VND; over 150K is overcharging REFUSE off-app deals from Grab drivers — re-book in app instead
scams.location: District 1 taxi ranks, Ben Thanh Market curbside hails, Bui Vien Walking Street return rides, Tan Dinh Market, late-night hails from District 3 and District 5

scams.name: Bui Vien Walking Street Bar 'Hostess' 4M VND Extortion
scams.description: HCMC's Bui Vien Walking Street has a specific 2025-documented bar-extortion scam. r/VietNam 'Ho Chi Minh City Walking Street (Bùi Viện) 4 million VND Scam' (comments/1lf9jl6, 2025) is a named 2025 anchor: the scam runs nearly identically to the Hanoi Tinder bar extortion. A 'hostess' or 'friendly local' invites a solo male traveller to a bar just off the main Bui Vien strip; drinks arrive in bottle format with inflated 'hostess' rates; a 4,000,000+ VND (~$160 USD) bill arrives with bouncers near the exit. r/VietNam 'Got soft hustled at a bar in Ho Chi Minh City from a girl I' (comments/1lhlzy8, 2025) captures the 2025 'soft-hustle' variant: 'It's only 2M, you might be scammed but those scammers are very humane. Some, even Vietnamese were scammed there too. r/VietNam 'Possible Bar Scam? Going to Vietnam soon and matched a' (comments/z00xdg) documents the dating-app pipeline: 'It's not a scam as such. But they are bar girls whose job it is to get you into the bar, have you' spend on overpriced drinks. The bars add 'drinks to your tab and argue with you if you' dispute per r/VietNam 'Ho Chi Minh City Walking Street (Bùi Viện) 4 million VND Scam' (comments/1lf9jl6, 2025). r/VietNam 'Scam operation in HCMC' (comments/1e92eov) names the operational pattern as 'Vietnamese bars are all about scamming you.' For male travellers of any age visiting Bui Vien, the defence is absolute: (1) NEVER follow a 'friendly local' or hostess into a side-street bar you didn't choose yourself; (2) verify the venue on Google Maps — fewer than 20 reviews or generic 5-star text = scam venue; (3) never order drinks without prices listed; (4) never let 'hostesses' join the table — this triggers premium-bottle charges; (5) if trapped with an inflated bill, refuse to pay the unjustified amount, pay what drinks were actually worth (30,000–80,000 VND each) and call HCMC Tourist Police (+84 28 3838 2990); (6) for a genuine Bui Vien experience, stay on the main pedestrian strip where bars have posted prices on outdoor menus.
scams.avoidance: NEVER follow a 'friendly local' or hostess to a bar you didn't choose yourself Verify venue on Google Maps — fewer than 20 reviews or generic 5-star = scam venue Never order drinks without prices listed Never let 'hostesses' join the table — triggers premium-bottle charges If trapped, pay honest rate (30K–80K VND/drink) and call HCMC Tourist Police (+84 28 3838 2990)
scams.location: Bui Vien Walking Street (Pham Ngu Lao / District 1 backpacker area), side-street bars with 'hostess' girls approaching solo male travellers, dark-alley karaoke venues off the main strip

scams.name: District 1 Motorbike Bag Snatch & Phone Grab
scams.description: HCMC's motorbike bag-snatch problem is more severe than Hanoi's and is a particular risk for older travellers who may not react fast enough. r/VietNam 'Concerned about bag snatchers and pickpockets on my' (comments/1gii41b, 2024) captures the stakes: 'I've heard countless accounts of people being dragged down the tarmac by bag snatchers on motorbikes' — the physical risk is real. r/VietNam 'Moped following me at night in the dark in HCMC?' (comments/1ncdomn, 2025) is a named 2025 first-person account: 'Though Vietnam is generally extremely safe, drive-by bag/phone snatching is it totally a thing, espe' cially at night. r/VietNam 'Is snatch theft still a thing in ho Chi Minh City?' (comments/1dili1v, 2024) documents the escalation: 'I saw one case last year, the theft snatch a lady gold necklace on motorbike. When she turned away, she was pulled off her feet. r/VietNam 'Definitely Vietnam is not as safe as you might think' (comments/1s17w2d, 2025) is another 2025 first-person anchor documenting 'common in al' l major Vietnamese cities. r/solotravelVN 'How do you stay safe while solo traveling in Vietnam?' (comments/1po13ag, 2025) notes that while pickpockets don't mean unsafe, 'Traffic safety is on you. It's busy but people don't drive' to hit you — but motorbike snatches intentionally target pedestrians. For older travellers, the protective playbook: (1) NEVER carry a phone in your hand while walking — motorbikes snatch them from sidewalks, and grabbing on can pull you into traffic; (2) wear a zipped crossbody bag in front, never a shoulder bag hanging loose; (3) walk on the side of the sidewalk AWAY from the road (building side); (4) split valuables: passport + backup card in hotel safe, small cash + one card in front pocket; (5) avoid wearing visible gold jewellery; (6) at night in District 1 and District 3, use Grab rather than walking; (7) if a motorbike approaches unusually close, step toward a shop doorway; (8) file report at HCMC Tourist Police (+84 28 3838 2990) within 24 hours for insurance.
scams.avoidance: NEVER carry phone in hand while walking — motorbike snatch can pull you into traffic Wear zipped crossbody bag in front, never shoulder bag hanging loose Walk on building-side of sidewalk, away from road At night in District 1/3, use Grab rather than walking; avoid visible gold or expensive watches File report at HCMC Tourist Police (+84 28 3838 2990) within 24 hours for insurance
scams.location: District 1 sidewalks (especially Nguyen Hue walking street, Dong Khoi, Le Loi), Ben Thanh Market perimeter, motorbike-dense intersections, late-night walks in District 3

scams.name: Ben Thanh Market Tourist Overcharge & Saigon Square Confusion
scams.description: Ben Thanh Market is HCMC's most-visited tourist attraction — and its most-documented 2025 tourist-overcharge zone. r/VietNam 'First Time in Saigon! Any tips for Ben Thanh Market?' (comments/1ogf62h, 2025) is blunt: 'Ben Thanh market is a total scam. Everything is prices between 3 to' 5x fair market. r/VietNam 'Saigon Square is what tourists think Ben Thanh Market is' (comments/1n9nxdg, 2025) is a named 2025 anchor explaining the community's fix: Saigon Square (the shopping centre directly across from Ben Thanh) is where locals actually buy clothes, bags, and souvenirs at honest prices, while Ben Thanh operates on pure tourist inflation. r/VietNam 'Bought coffee from the local market. Scammed or got' (comments/1gzjb5v, 2025) documents the specific coffee-shop scam: tourists buy 'Trung Nguyen coffee' from Ben Thanh vendors at 5x legitimate shop prices. The authentic Trung Nguyen store is on Nguyen Hue and has posted prices. r/VietNam 'HCMC - scams, scams and not scams' (comments/1os81k3, 2025) frames the broader market dynamic: the vendors aren't committing fraud per se — they're selling real goods at tourist-inflated prices, but the social-pressure pricing and 'haggle down from 5x' model makes it a scam for anyone who doesn't know the local price floor. For older travellers, the practical rule: (1) Ben Thanh Market is a photo-stop, NOT a shopping destination — expect 3-5x markups and pushy vendors; (2) for clothes/bags/electronics, cross the road to Saigon Square (indoor, fixed prices, locals shop there); (3) for Trung Nguyen coffee, go to the official store on Nguyen Hue; (4) for food, eat at the posted-price food stalls inside Ben Thanh (stall numbers visible) rather than tourist-facing restaurants on the market perimeter; (5) if you do buy at Ben Thanh, start negotiating at 30% of the quoted price; (6) never touch or try on items unless you intend to buy — vendors lock you into a 'purchase obligation' via social pressure.
scams.avoidance: Treat Ben Thanh as a photo-stop, not a shopping destination For clothes/bags/electronics, go to Saigon Square across the road (fixed prices, locals shop) For Trung Nguyen coffee, visit the OFFICIAL store on Nguyen Hue (posted prices) If you must buy at Ben Thanh, start negotiating at 30% of quoted price Never touch or try on items unless you intend to buy — social pressure activates
scams.location: Ben Thanh Market (District 1), Saigon Square shopping centre across the road, pushy vendors at market entrances, 'fake Trung Nguyen coffee' sellers

scams.name: HCMC Booking.com / Agoda Off-Platform Payment Fraud
scams.description: HCMC has a specific 2025-documented hotel-booking fraud ecosystem. r/VietNam '[Warning] Scam hotel chain in Ho Chi Minh City' (comments/1m8qxgt, 2025) is a named 2025 anchor: 'My partner and I recently had a terrible experience with a hotel scam in Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam — booked through Booking.com but then received off-platform payment requests that turned out to be phishing. r/VietNam 'Hotel payment - Is this legitimate?' (comments/1jookvm, 2025) captures the broader pattern: 'Pretty common scam. If you get a message from Agoda or Booking with a link to a different site, ignore it.' r/VietNam '🚨 SCAM ALERT in Hanoi – Booking.com' (comments/1jytqu8, 2025) documents the same pattern operating in Hanoi — the ecosystem is cross-city. r/VietNam 'Scam' (comments/1mc8lt8, 2025) records a hotel-specific extortion: 'The hotel staff claimed there were black marks on the bedsheets and asked them to pay 1,320,000 VND. When they asked to see evidence, it disappeared — a post-checkout extortion pattern that requires a documented denuncia to dispute via credit card. For older travellers booking HCMC hotels, the defensive playbook: (1) ANY message requesting additional payment off-platform is a scam — legitimate Booking.com/Agoda hotels collect at check-in or via card-on-file; (2) if you receive a WhatsApp or email claiming 'verification issues,' contact the platform support via the APP — never click message links; (3) refuse Bizum, Western Union, cryptocurrency, or unfamiliar-gateway payment requests; (4) verify hotel bookings a week before arrival by calling the property from the number on the OFFICIAL hotel website (not the number in the email); (5) at check-out, photograph the room state (especially bedsheets, carpets, bathroom) to defend against post-stay 'damage' claims per r/VietNam 'Scam' (comments/1mc8lt8, 2025); (6) if defrauded, file a credit card chargeback immediately and report to Booking.com/Agoda fraud channels.
scams.avoidance: Treat ANY off-platform payment request as a scam — legitimate hotels collect at check-in For 'verification' messages, contact Booking.com/Agoda support via the APP — never click message links Refuse Bizum, Western Union, cryptocurrency, or unfamiliar-gateway payment requests At check-out, photograph room state (bedsheets, carpet, bathroom) to defend against 'damage' claims If defrauded, file credit card chargeback immediately and report to platform fraud channels
scams.location: Online — Booking.com and Agoda HCMC hotel listings, WhatsApp follow-up 'host' messages after booking, fake 'payment verification' emails, specific scam-hotel chains flagged
